sources.entry: C#: _Building a BitTorrent client from scratch in C#_

summary.title: BitTorrent: Building a BitTorrent client from scratch in C#
summary.one_liner: You learn how the BitTorrent protocol works (torrents, trackers, peers, pieces) and how to implement its BEncoding format and torrent parsing in C#.
takeaways: BitTorrent splits files into pieces that peers exchange, with SHA1 hashes used to verify each piece.
BEncoding has four types (strings as byte arrays, integers as long, lists, and dictionaries with sorted keys), and the page shows C# encoder and decoder code for them.
A torrent file's info section is hashed with SHA1 to produce the infohash that identifies the torrent.
Testing a client needs a tracker such as OpenTracker plus existing clients like Transmission or Deluge on separate machines.
summary.summary: The author explains the BitTorrent protocol at a conceptual level, covering peer-to-peer sharing, seeders and leechers, trackers, and how the protocol evolved from Napster. The page then walks through a test run with OpenTracker and Transmission to confirm the setup works. The main body builds a BEncoding encoder and decoder in C# (strings as byte arrays, longs, lists, sorted dictionaries) and begins modelling the torrent file structure with Torrent, FileItem and Tracker classes, plus infohash and piece/block handling. The page is cut off before the protocol and networking sections of the project.
